To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) leak and isotopic disequilibrum artefacts are important in Δ measurements with clamp-on cuvettes, and that (2) they can be minimized by careful experimental design and fully corrected with protocols described here.

(1) leak errors and isotopic disequilbria are potential sources of errors on Δ; (2) leak coefficients for (12) C and (13) C can be determined with the same leaves as those used for Δ measurements; (3) leak errors in Δ are fully corrected with the leak coefficients determined on these leaves; and (4) isotopic disequilibria can be analysed in terms of partitioning between net photosynthesis in light and dark respiration.

(a) leaks of (12) CO 2 and (13 CO 2 were identical, (b) leak coefficients were higher with leaves in clamp-on cuvettes than without leaves, (c) leaks generated errors in Δ that could be corrected with leak coefficients, (d) isotopic disequilbria between net photosynthetic and dark respiratory fluxes were observed in full light, (e) isotopic disequalibria could be corrected to obtain partitioning of net fluxes
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to correct Δ values for leak artefacts.
the quantification of artefacts and flux partitioning during combined measurements of leaf gas exchange and Δ, and provides new protocols to correct for these phenomena.
the quantification, minimization, and correction of leak and isotopic disequlibrium artefacts in clamp-on leaf cuvettes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leak artefacts can be corrected, but the isotopic disequilibrium is a real phenomenon that cannot be eliminated.

leak artefacts can be minimized by careful design of cuvette and leaf clamps.
